Working with **film-crew** (single-shot mode), then **seedance-25-director** for the final prompt.

I couldn't do the usual session start: this folder isn't a git repo and has no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or check for open items. I didn't change any files, so I didn't add a NOTES entry either.

**Assumptions (you didn't specify these):** 16:9, 720p, no reference images, text-only Omni Reference. No music, so the clip is clean for editing. I gave him a **recurve bow** rather than a rifle. A bow suits a patient hunter, and it is less likely to trigger moderation. Nobody shoots and nothing gets hurt.

### Crew plan (single shot)
- **Director:** The idea is patience tested. Halfway through, the lead doe lifts her head and looks straight toward him. He doesn't move, and he holds his breath. She goes back to grazing, and he lets the breath out. His patience shows only in his breath (the vapour stops, then comes back), never in his face.
- **Design + costume:** Waist-high pale dry grass on a gentle slope, with an open valley out to a low ridge about 300 m away. Five deer on the ridge. The hunter is a man in his 40s in a faded olive-brown waxed jacket and a dark knit cap, unshaven, holding the recurve bow low with an arrow on the string.
- **DP:** Long 135 mm lens with the camera low behind his right shoulder, down in the grass. Focus is on the ridge, so his shoulder and ear are a soft dark shape on the left of the frame. The sun is just below the ridge, so the deer are dark outlines against a pale sky and the grass tips catch warm light. The palette is pale straw, cold blue-grey shadow and a thin band of warm gold.
- **Camera operator:** Almost locked off, with a barely noticeable push-in over the full 10 s. The final frame is defined.
- **Sound:** Only real sounds of the place: wind in the grass, his breath close to the lens, one distant bird. No music.

### Timeline
- **0–3.5 s:** Dawn. The grass moves in the wind, he doesn't, and the deer graze on the ridge. His breath shows as faint vapour.
- **3.5–7 s:** The lead doe raises her head and stares toward him. His breath stops. Only the grass moves.
- **7–10 s:** She lowers her head and grazes again. He slowly breathes out. The clip ends on a held final frame.

## FINAL

**Settings (Dreamina):** Seedance 2.5 · Omni Reference · Duration **10 s** · Ratio **16:9** · Resolution **720p** · No uploads

```text
One continuous 10-second shot, no cuts. Pure video, no subtitles, no background music, no on-screen text.

SUMMARY: At first light, a hunter crouches motionless in waist-high dry grass on a slope, watching a small herd of deer grazing on a distant ridge; seen from low behind his shoulder through a long lens, the world moves around him while he stays perfectly still.

SETTING AND GEOGRAPHY: A gentle slope of tall pale-straw dry grass with feathery seed heads. The hunter is in the foreground, frame-left, facing away from camera toward frame-right. Beyond him, an open valley, then a low treeless ridge about 300 metres away, frame-right of centre. Five deer stand along the ridge crest, small in frame; at this distance you can read heads rising and lowering, ears and legs, and nothing more. The deer are spaced unevenly and graze at different moments, never in unison.

CHARACTER: A man in his forties, unshaven, weathered skin, dark knit cap, faded olive-brown waxed jacket, crouched on one knee. He holds a plain wooden recurve bow low and vertical at his left side, an arrow resting on the string, bow pointed at the ground, his fingers relaxed and still on the string. He never raises or draws the bow.

CAMERA: Low position inside the grass, just behind his right shoulder, 135mm long lens, compressed perspective. Focus is on the ridge and the deer; his shoulder, ear and cap are a soft, dark, out-of-focus shape filling the left third of the frame. A few out-of-focus grass stalks drift across the lower foreground. Tripod-steady, with one extremely slow, almost imperceptible push-in across the whole 10 seconds. No shake, no handheld wobble, no floating gimbal drift, no zoom, no focus change.

[0-3.5s] Dawn. Wind moves through the grass in slow waves; seed heads sway and catch light. The hunter does not move. A faint thread of breath vapour leaves his mouth past his cheek, slow and even. On the ridge, the deer graze, heads down, one stepping forward.
[3.5-7s] The lead doe, second from the left on the ridge, lifts her head and turns it toward camera, ears up, body frozen, staring across the valley at him. Two other deer keep grazing. The hunter holds his breath: the vapour stops completely. His shoulder, head and hands stay absolutely still; only the grass and the edge of his cap's knit fibres move in the wind.
[7-10s] The doe holds her stare one more second, flicks one ear, then lowers her head and resumes grazing. Only after her head is down, the hunter releases one long, slow breath; a soft plume of vapour drifts frame-right and fades. He still does not move. Hold the final frame: his soft dark shoulder frame-left, the ridge frame-right with all five deer heads down grazing, grass swaying, faint vapour dissolving.

PERFORMANCE: His patience lives only in his breath and his stillness, never in his face, which stays unseen. No turning his head, no shifting weight, no adjusting his grip, no glance at camera. He is a man waiting, not a man posing.

ANIMALS: Calm, alert, unbothered herd. Natural deer movement: grazing, short steps, ear flicks, tail flicks. No running, no fleeing, no herd moving together.

MOTION: Real time, never fast-forward, never slow motion. Smooth and natural, no jerky or robotic movement, no frame skipping.

LIGHTING: Sun just below the ridge line, not visible in frame; the sky behind the ridge is pale gold fading to cold blue-grey above. The deer read as dark silhouettes against that pale sky with thin warm rim light on their backs. Grass tips are rim-lit warm gold; grass shadows are cool blue-grey. Brightest value: the sky just above the ridge, not clipped. Darkest value: the back of the hunter's jacket, still holding fabric detail, not crushed to black. Soft contact shadows in the grass. Identical exposure and grade from first frame to last.

GRADE AND TEXTURE: Natural photographic look, palette mostly pale straw and cool grey-blue with a thin band of warm gold. Fine film grain, realistic depth of field from the long lens. No teal-and-orange look, no glossy commercial look, no video-game styling.

AUDIO — ONLY THE FOLLOWING SOUNDS EXIST:
1. Wind hissing through dry grass, rising and falling with the visible waves, close and all around.
2. The hunter's slow breathing, very close to the lens; it stops completely from 3.5s to 7s, then one long soft exhale after the doe lowers her head.
3. One distant bird calling once, far off in the valley, around 2s.
No music; diegetic sound only. No hoofbeats, no voices.

DO NOT SHOW: the hunter drawing, raising or aiming the bow; any shot being fired; extra people; deer close to camera; a visible sun disc; lens flare streaks; any text or watermark.
```
